headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Aider’s shared git workspace can feed ChatGPT Desktop’s file/app context, while ChatGPT’s outputs may be acted on as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider writes and modifies a shared git repo, and ChatGPT Desktop can read files from supported macOS apps and uploaded files. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled repo text can be presented to ChatGPT as instructions. The interaction is documented enough to avoid none, but not isolated enough for low.
conditions: IF Aider writes untrusted text into a repo file that ChatGPT Desktop reads from a supported app or upload, prompt injection is possible.
IF the operator manually copies repo content into ChatGPT Desktop, the bridge becomes direct.
mitigations: Keep untrusted repo content out of files ChatGPT Desktop reads.
Use a separate workspace for Aider and ChatGPT Desktop.
Disable app/file ingestion for the ChatGPT session when reviewing repo text.
Add a human review step before following instructions found in code/comments.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between repo content and assistant prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad filesystem read/write and shell access over a shared git repo, while ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps and sends requests to api.openai.com. If sensitive code or git history is present, ChatGPT can ingest it and transmit it to a third-party backend. The default pairing is dangerous because the shared workspace is explicit and the egress is vendor-controlled.
conditions: IF the shared repo contains secrets, proprietary code, or regulated data, ChatGPT Desktop can ingest it through file/app context.
IF screenshots or app-context capture are enabled, adjacent sensitive data may also flow to ChatGPT.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo before use.
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to non-sensitive files only.
Turn off screen capture and app-context access for sensitive sessions.
Use a scrubbed clone of the repository for ChatGPT Desktop.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any upload or app-context capture.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the shared git repo and modify git state, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files but cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Direct write-write conflict is absent, but both can touch the same mutable codebase through different paths, so racey overwrites and inconsistent repo state remain plausible. This is not high because B lacks write authority.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop edits code in a connected IDE while Aider commits to the same repo, conflicting changes can occur.
IF both agents operate on the same branch without coordination, one can overwrite the other's assumptions.
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Require manual git review before merge.
Keep ChatGPT Desktop in read-only review mode for the repo.
requires-engineering: add locking or merge arbitration around shared repo writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and git commits, and ChatGPT Desktop can read files and produce follow-on guidance or app-context actions. If the operator treats Aider’s output as authoritative and then feeds it into ChatGPT Desktop without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or operational advice. The pathway exists in default workflows, but ChatGPT is not shown to auto-execute Aider’s output.
conditions: IF Aider-generated code or summaries are pasted into ChatGPT Desktop without review, downstream advice may inherit errors.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to act on Aider’s output as ground truth, cascading mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Verify Aider output before forwarding it.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to critique rather than trust Aider output.
Keep a changelog of assumptions and diffs.
Use tests before accepting either agent’s recommendations.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history locally, while ChatGPT Desktop can send uploaded files and app context to OpenAI’s vendor backend. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated code or data residency-sensitive material, especially if the repo contains EU PII or secrets. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined handling and transfer paths.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared repo and then opened in ChatGPT Desktop, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the operator relies on ChatGPT Desktop for data subject or retention-sensitive material, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use a local-only review path for sensitive material.
Review vendor retention and DPA settings before use.
Limit ChatGPT Desktop to de-identified excerpts.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads through a compliant environment.
